title: Product PRD: Unified Inference 2.0 — Overview, Requirements, Design, Roadmap, Pricing & Release Notes
author: Aisha Nair
body:
Overview

Summary:
Unified Inference 2.0 is the next major product release that unifies hosting, dedicated, and private deployment experiences under a single developer surface while improving cost controls, reliability, and observability. This PRD consolidates product goals, high-level requirements, design decisions, roadmap milestones, pricing/packaging options, and release notes for the 2.0 launch window.

Goals (top-level):
- Provide a consistent API and rollout model across Hosted API, Dedicated, and Private deployments.
- Reduce average per-token cost by 30% for typical production workloads through batching, quantization recommendations, and smart routing.
- Achieve 99.95% regional uptime SLA for paid Dedicated customers with automated fallbacks.
- Improve developer observability: per-route latency and cost breakdowns, built-in regression detection for prompt sets.

Success metrics (tracked in Redwood Console):
- Latency: p95 for text-generation <= 450ms for 8k context L/16k-like sequence on curated workload.
- Cost: 30% reduction in tokens/$ for top 10 customers in beta using Optimize suggestions.
- Reliability: <0.05% sustained errors per route over 24h for Dedicated customers.
- Adoption: 200 production customers migrated to Unified Inference within 3 months of GA.

Scope
- In scope:
  - Unified API surface (text generation, chat, embeddings, reranking) with consistent model version pinning and rollout semantics.
  - Runtime features: automatic prefix/KV caching, workload-aware batching, quantization profiles, and smart routing by policy.
  - Console: per-route dashboards, cost breakdowns, and model impact evals.
  - Pricing & packaging for Hosted and Dedicated; baseline guidance for Private deployments.
- Out of scope for 2.0:
  - Full on-prem install automation for every OS/version (addressed in subsequent private deployment patch).
  - Marketplace billing integrations beyond core cloud marketplaces (post-GA).

Requirements
Functional requirements (FR):
- FR-01: API parity — All existing Redwood API endpoints must behave identically across deployment modes (owner: api-platform).
- FR-02: Model pinning and rollouts — Allow per-customer per-route model pinning and gradual canary rollouts (owner: product).
- FR-03: Cost suggestions — Provide model/quantization/batching recommendations tied to historical workload (owner: optimize-team).
- FR-04: Observability — Per-token latency and cost breakdown and prompt-set based regression alerts (owner: console-team).

Non-functional requirements (NFR):
- NFR-01 (Reliability): 99.95% regional uptime SLA for Dedicated (owner: eng-sre).
- NFR-02 (Performance): Support p95 <= 450ms text generation for target workload profile on baseline Dedicated config (owner: serving-runtime).
- NFR-03 (Security): End-to-end encryption for Private deployments with KMS integration (owner: security-and-compliance).
- NFR-04 (Scalability): Autoscaling to support 4x baseline burst traffic with graceful fallbacks (owner: eng-infra).

Design overview

High-level components:
- Developer API Layer: REST/SDK endpoints with feature flags for rollout semantics and per-request routing metadata.
- Control Plane: Rollout manager, model catalog, billing hooks, and policy engine.
- Serving Runtime: GPU-optimized inference engine implementing KV cache sharing, continuous batching, quantization-friendly execution paths, and kernel selection logic.
- Smart Router: Policy-based request routing (latency-first, cost-first, region-preferred) and fallback to compatible model variants.
- Console / Observability: Per-route dashboards, traces, token cost breakdowns, and eval integration for regression detection.

API contract example (excerpt):
- Endpoint: POST /v1/generate
- Payload: {"route_id":"string", "input":"string|array","model":"redwood/<model>:<version>", "routing_policy":"latency|cost|region"}
- Response: streaming tokens, final metadata with token_count, cost_estimate_usd, model_version, trace_id

Design decisions and trade-offs:
- Decision: Use model-variant fallback vs. degrade to CPU — we prefer fallback to a quantized variant on GPU to preserve latency while sacrificing some quality (trade-off: minor quality regression vs. large latency increase if CPU fallback).
- Decision: Granular per-route rollouts are critical for customers with different SLOs; we expose weighted canaries at 1/5/25/50/100% steps.
- Decision: Incremental rollout of caching logic with opt-in per-customer to mitigate cache pollution during migration.

Detailed runtime notes:
- Continuous batching parameters: default batch window 8ms, dynamic up to 35ms when throughput detected.
- KV cache retention: default 30 minutes per route; configurable per-customer via console.
- Quantization profiles: supported profiles: q4_0, q4_1, q8_0; Optimize will recommend profiles by examining token distribution and output fidelity metrics.

Rollout plan (GA -> production)

1) Internal dogfood (2 weeks)
   - Migrate internal test teams to Unified Inference 2.0. Verify p95 latency, cost delta, and regressions on curated prompt suites.
2) Developer beta (4 weeks)
   - Invite 50 customers (mix of AI-native startups and platform teams) with support engineering involvement.
   - Canary rollout semantics: 1%, 5%, 25%, 50%, 100% by route. Monitor: error rate, latency p95/p99, cost delta, prompt-set accuracy.
3) Early access for Dedicated customers (6 weeks)
   - Offer migration plan and performance tuning for Dedicated customers with SLA targets.
4) GA public launch
   - Marketing + docs + SDK updates.

Monitoring and rollback criteria:
- Automatic rollback if 5xx rate increases by >200% sustained for 10 minutes OR prompt-set accuracy drops by >3% for two consecutive eval runs.
- Manual rollback if p95 latency exceeds target by 50% for 15 minutes or customer reports severity-1 issues.

| Q4 2027 | Ecosystem | Marketplace billing, third-party integrations, multi-region resilience improvements |

Pricing & packaging notes

Principles: keep a PLG-friendly free tier for experimentation, offer committed capacity for predictable Dedicated pricing, and provide enterprise packaging for Private with support SLAs.

Proposed pricing tiers (summary):
- Free (trial): 100k tokens/month, basic console, community support.
- Pay-as-you-go (Hosted): $0.0006 per token for gen-high (baseline) and $0.0002 per embedding unit.
- Committed Dedicated: base reservation + per-token overage. Example: $10k/month reserved capacity for 10M tokens/month effective floor price $0.0005/token; overage $0.00045/token.
- Private Enterprise: Platform fee + per-seat OR committed throughput; KMS/HSM add-on priced separately.

Discounts and incentives:
- 10–20% discount for annual committed contracts.
- Migration credits for early adopters (up to 3 months of base reservation).

Billing configuration table:
| Packaging | Billing model | Key terms |
| Free | Flat free tier | 100k tokens/mo |
| PAYG | Per-token | No minimum, card billing |
| Dedicated | Reserved + overage | Monthly/annual commitment, overage rate, SLA |
| Private | Platform + support | Platform fee, installation charge, support tiers |

Release notes (2.0 GA)
- New: Unified API surface across Hosted/Dedicated/Private.
- New: Per-route model pinning and weighted canary rollouts (1/5/25/50/100%).
- New: Console cost breakdowns by token and prompt set; built-in regression alerts.
- New: Optimize v1 recommendations for batching and quantization with per-customer guidance.
- Improved: Serving runtime kernel selection and continuous batching decreased median latency by ~18% in internal benchmarks.
- Known issues: Some 3rd-party telemetry integrations require minor adapter changes (listed in related_pages).
